title: SK2P: centred double decrease
subtitle: A double decrease that removes two stitches and centres the result.
excerpt: SK2P (slip 1, knit 2 together, pass slipped stitch over) reduces the stitch count by two and places the central stitch over the decreased pair, creating a vertical line in the fabric.
sourceNotes: Double decrease methods documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), lace chapter. Weldon's lace series (1888 onward) uses the equivalent 'sl1, k2tog, psso' phrasing.

glossaryTerms.definition: Slip 1, knit 2 together, pass slipped stitch over: a centred double decrease that removes two stitches from the stitch count, leaving the central stitch sitting on top of the pair. Creates a vertical decrease line in lace patterns. Also written s2kp or cdd.
Any decrease that reduces the stitch count by two rather than one. SK2P, S2KP2, and k3tog are all double decreases.

content.text: SK2P (slip 1, knit 2 together, pass slipped stitch over) is a centred
that places the centre stitch on top of the two decreased stitches, producing a vertical column in lace.

reduces the count by two (one slipped + two worked into one = a net loss of two). It is paired with two yarn overs in lace to maintain stitch count, forming the triple-column leaf or fern that characterises many Victorian lace patterns. Difficulty: intermediate.
DK yarn and 4 mm needles with a few rows worked
Work to the position of the decrease.
Slip one stitch knitwise from the left to the right needle.
Knit the next two stitches together (k2tog).
Insert the left needle into the slipped stitch on the right needle and pass it over the k2tog stitch and off the needle.
One stitch remains where three were. Stitch count reduced by two.

SK2P forms the spine of many lace leaf patterns, where the central vein is a column of double decreases flanked by yarn overs. Victorian Shetland lace shawls use SK2P (written sl1-k2tog-psso) throughout their border designs. It also appears at hat crowns where rapid reduction is needed in a single row, and in short-row shaping where two stitches must be removed at a point.

items.symptom: Centre stitch leans instead of sitting vertically
items.cause: Slipping the stitch purlwise rather than knitwise
items.fix: The slip in SK2P must be knitwise. A purlwise slip at step 2 shifts the lean of the resulting stitch.

items.symptom: Count reduced by three instead of two
items.cause: Knitting three stitches together (k3tog) instead of following the slip-then-k2tog sequence
items.fix: SK2P removes exactly two stitches (three in, one out). If the count is off by more, recount from the beginning of the row.
